title: Moonshift closure and deferred triage notes — 2027-10-20
content:
Shift summary (19:00-07:00 local)

Quick summary:
- Several small escalations stacked into a single customer-impact window between ~01:10–01:45. Root symptoms: elevated p95 token latency on hosted-api (route /v1/stream) coincident with backend cache flapping and a low-capacity gyro-dedicated pool hitting soft limits.
- No full P0; customers saw transient 503s and stream truncations. Automatic fallback routing mitigated some impact.
- Primary unresolved: intermittent KV cache eviction thrashing leading to CPU spikes on the inference proxies and a slow leak of capacity in pool gyro-dedicated-03.

Timeline and actions (brief):
- 19:05 — shift start, checked runbook health dashboard, all green. Noted PR 998 staging restart scheduled for 10/21.
- 22:40 — alert: hosted-api p95 token latency > 800ms for EU region. Initial triage: coincident increase in redis-metrics->evictions.
- 22:45 — escalated to infra-engineering (Diego) to validate redis cluster alerts and eviction thresholds. Slack thread #ops-nightwatch created: thread id OPS-ntwk-6521.
- 23:05 — mitigations applied: temporarily increased cache ttl on prefix-cache service (service: prefix-cache-v2) to reduce churn; fallback routing rule enabled to route low-priority traffic to smaller model variant (routed to model: rw-lite-1b).
- 00:40 — observed sustained CPU on inference-proxy-*. cpu top shows frequent ctx-switching; suspected mem pressure + KV churn.
- 01:15 — customer reports of truncated streams; pagerduty incident SRE-1423 triggered and acknowledged.
- 01:25 — ramped up dedicated pool gyro-dedicated-04 by +2 replicas (manual spin-up) as quick capacity buffer; some recovery in 503s but latency remained elevated.
- 02:10 — rolling restart of prefix-cache instances (graceful drain) per temporary mitigation; rollback plan prepared in case of regression.
- 03:00 — stabilization: p95 fell back to ~350–420ms; streams returning to normal.
- 05:00 — follow-up notes compiled, deferred remediation tracked as SRE-1423 and infra backlog item INFRA-2876.

Tech details and evidence:
- Metrics: hosted-api p95 spike 800->1200ms at 22:40; token-generation error-rate spiked 0.1%->1.7%; 503 spikes matched KV eviction bursts.
- Proxies: inference-proxy logs show frequent redis EXPIRE misses followed by heavy KV reloads. Example log snippet (redacted):
  [2027-10-20T22:42:18Z] proxy-12 ERROR kv-cache miss for key-prefix user:ctx:abcd -> backend lookup (1.2s)
- Redis stats snapshot (22:43): evicted_keys: 1287/min, used_memory_rss_peak 75% of node, instantaneous_ops_per_sec 4.1k
- Capacity pool: gyro-dedicated-03 shows steady decline in available tokens reported by autoscaler; investigation suggests a leaking long-lived session process (ticket INFRA-2876 created).

Runbook gaps we hit (actionable):
- No explicit step in cache-eviction runbook for when eviction rate > 500/min and p95>600ms. We improvised with TTL bump and restart; standard playbook should include: check eviction rate, NEXUS failover state, step-by-step TTL increase, and safe rolling restart thresholds.
- Fallback routing rules exist but are not documented with exact priority mappings for 'low-priority' traffic. Need a matrix: route->model variant mapping + impact table.
- Dedicated-pool leak detection: autoscaler metrics are noisy and there is no runbook entry to run a quick process-scan and orphaned-KV cleanup.

Immediate action items (owners and ETA):
- SRE: add short runbook appendix for 'cache-eviction surge' with explicit thresholds and quick mitigation commands. Owner: Samira Patel. ETA: 2027-10-25.
- Infra: investigate leaking session processes on gyro-dedicated-03 and add liveness probe tuning. Owner: Connor Blake. ETA: 2027-10-22 (investigation start)
- Serving-runtime: add telemetry to inference-proxy to emit kv-eviction-cause metric (soft vs forced). Owner: Eve Liu. ETA: 2027-11-02.
- Product: decide and document which routes are "low-priority" and safe to downgrade automatically. Product liaison: Maya Chen. ETA: 2027-10-28.

Commands & quick recovery snippets used (notes copied here for next shift):
- Check redis eviction rate: redis-cli -h $REDIS_HOST INFO stats | egrep 'evicted_keys|instantaneous_ops_per_sec'
- Temporarily increase prefix cache TTL (k8s): kubectl set env deployment/prefix-cache-v2 CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=1200 -n hosted-api && rollout status deploy/prefix-cache-v2 -n hosted-api
- Graceful restart sequence: kubectl rollout restart deployment/prefix-cache-v2 -n hosted-api --wait=true
- Scale dedicated pool quickly (kustomize / api): infractl pool scale --pool gyro-dedicated-04 --replicas +2 --reason "night buffer"

Deferred items for follow-up (carryover):
- INFRA-2876: analyze and close the leaking session process; possibly add pre-emptive cleanup job. (Priority: high)
- SRE-1423: create a canonical runbook appendix and add tests in staging to simulate eviction storms. (Priority: high)
- Create a small synthetic test that simulates prefix-cache churn and confirm the fallback routing triggers as expected. (Priority: medium)

Notes to next shift (concise):
- Priority one: confirm INFRA-2876 triage started; check if any core-dumps or heap-growth traces exist on gyro-dedicated-03.
- Priority two: update runbook doc link (below) with the temporary TTL tweak we used; we need a safe rollback threshold.
- If p95 > 600ms again: follow new temporary flow — bump TTL, enable fallback routing, scale a dedicated pool, prepare for rolling restart.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Is TTL bump a long-term safe mitigation? (We used it as a short-term buffer but it may increase memory; need product input on acceptable cache staleness.)
- Should fallback routing be automatic at certain SLO breach thresholds? If yes, what is the acceptable business tradeoff?

References / links used during triage:
- Pagerduty incident: SRE-1423
- Infra PR (staging restart scheduling): github.com/redwood/infra/pull/998
- Runbook seed: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=8932
- Slack thread: #ops-nightwatch (thread OPS-ntwk-6521)

Sticky notes / notes-to-self (choppy):
- remember to add a small test in chaos-lab that runs a 5m eviction storm profile (copy from old chaos repo snippet).
- check telemetry retention: we had only 7 days of raw proxy logs; extend to 14 for these incidents. cost win? bring up with observability.

Signature:
Samira Patel (on-call)
Diego Martinez (infra assist)
Connor Blake (manual scaling)
Eve Liu (serving-runtime)

End of shift.
